Quadrivus hovered inside the Temple of Roxxarum, waiting beside the slab on which Iskandar slept. The Holnareem of the temple had sent news that Iskandar was stirring, and he had come to investigate. After all, they city, and he himself, owed much to the forgemaster.

Iskandar's wounded, fleshy sections were covered with bandages. Quadrivus could only assume that those would be weak points, capable of inducing great pain if struck. They would need proper dressings, but that could wait until Iskandar awakened. After all, Sentenza had no greater smith than its forgemaster.

As Iskandar's eyes fluttered, Quadrivus allowed his head to assume a face, full of familiar features, it would do no good to scare him further by appearing as a faceless apparition. Mustering a smile, Quadrivus uttered a greetings, and a smooth, soothing voice wafted through the halls of the Temple.

*"Hello, Iskandar, my old friend. It has been too long. I must say, it is great to see that you are alive. Some citizens were beginning to think something horrible has happened!"*

Iskandar rose, groaning, and with a clearly displeased expression on his face. He spend the next few minutes stretching, noticing the many bandages on his form, then spoke.

"Did you have the brilliant idea of setting me to rest on this stone slab? Is there no softer bed in all Sentenza?" Iskandar pouted, a little grumpy, then flashed a slight grin to show he was joking.

*"No, I'm afraid not. Poor living accommodations for a hero, we are well aware, but before the war there was little use for beds in Sentenza."* Quadrivus helped Iskandar to his feet, struggling visibly to pull up his immense form.

"How fairs the city?"

*"Oh Sentenza has recovered well, the Flora have settled a new city to the North, and even the Crystal Scar is brimming with new life! It is glorious in these parts. We have begun to spread, and although there have been certain crimes, looting, and a bit of general tomfoolery, most of it has quieted down. It's you we're worried about."

They were walking now, down the hall from where Iskandar was left to rest towards his great anvil. They stopped by a large mirror, almost as tall as the hall itself. Iskandar gazed sideways, and peeled away his bandages. With a startle, he jumped a foot into the air, then smashed the mirror with his bare hands.

"So it is true..." Iskandar muttered darkly, quietly, as if to himself.

*"What is true, what is the problem Iskandar?"*

Iskandar winced, it was impossible to hide your concern from the Spectra, such a nosy people, and so perceptive in a way that many races weren't. It was, unsettling at times.

"None. Of. Your. Business." Iskandar snarled through gritted teeth.

*"Oh don't be silly, of course it is my business. After all, you sacrificed much for the sake of the city, whatever is your concern is our concern."*

Iskandar was once again at an impasse. He had the strength and speed to bash the spectre aside and hide away from the questioning, but it would be futile. He could run, but he would be found. He couldn't run anymore, it was time to face the truth.

"I am a... Fleshchanged. I am unholy, a monster that will destroy everything I hold dear right when everything is at its most perfect." Iskandar hung his head. "I should flee, far from here, so that what I saw could never come to pass."

A long pause settled.

*"And why would that matter?"* A soft voice, as if it floated on the breeze, shattered the silence. On it was a note of certainty, a note of reflection. With a single phrase, Iskandar's eyes widened, and stood in stunned silence.

"Why everything, this changes EVERYTHING. Don't you understand what I am?"

*"You are a hero who fought to save the flora, who fought to save the people you brought to this fair land. You are a valiant solder who fought for the cause of freedom. You are a forgemaster, a fine artisan, and a wielder of an extraordinary hammer. Even now, legends are told about your actions, about your bravery and valor and sacrifice. You ask me what you are, when you fail to see it yourself."*

Each word oozed with certainty, with truth, with conviction that few could muster. Strange creatures, to walk the path of uncertainty so certainly.

*"You may be fleshchanged, but you are Holnareem. The young ones admire you, the other smiths envy you. You are the ideal towards which they strive! Yet when you are brought to the flame you would just snivel and hide."*

A flash of rage, in both their eyes. For yet another moment, they sat still.

*"To me, you are Iskandar, master of the forge, wielder of the Mutriqat Alttakwin. You think you're such a monster, just go talk to one of the people you saved, see what they say."*

*"Remember, steel is tempered through the trial of fire. I expected more from you Iskandar. Steel grows stronger when it is passed through the flames, to see this reaction is... Disappointing."*

*"Please, take the day, relax. Your hammer is on your anvil, Phaedrus brought it here, just swooshed his hands and POOF, magic, the hammer was there. If you want to leave, come talk to me, if you want to stay, come talk to me. Or don't, it's your choice."*

Quadrivus silently floated forwards, leaving Iskandar behind.
